newsitem.title: USA: Illinois SRW wheat harvested at a record pace.
newsitem.headline: Illinois SRW wheat harvested at a record pace.

text.p: The Illinois soft red winter wheat crop was harvested at a record pace during the week ended Sunday, the Illinois Agricultural Statistics Service said.

The wheat was 85 percent harvested, above the 80 percent pace of last year and the average. Ninety-six percent of wheat was ripe, higher than last year's 93 percent but lower than the five-year average of 95 percent.
Lacking moisture, both the corn and soybean crops declined from week-ago levels, the report said.
Corn was rated two percent very poor, four percent poor, 25 fair, 56 percent good and 13 percent excellent.
Soybeans were rated two percent very poor, five percent poor, 31 fair, 53 percent good and nine percent excellent.
Soil moisture levels declined and were becoming a concern for farmers across the northern two-thirds of the state, the report said.
Topsoil moisture was rated 11 percent very short, 40 percent short, 46 percent adequate and three percent surplus.
